summary: Siegfried Lienhard was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna and completed his Habilitation at Stockholm University. He held professorships at Kiel University (1962–1968) and Stockholm University (1968–1990).

Sieglinde Dietz specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn under Michael Hahn in 1980 and held a post at the University of Göttingen, attested in 1990.
Signe Cohen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Ludo Rocher. She holds a post as professor at the University of Missouri.
Signe Howell was a scholar of religious studies who studied at SOAS University of London and the University of Oxford. She became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1989.

Silvia Luraghi is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Turin. She held positions at the University of Turin (~1987–1992), Università degli Studi Roma Tre (~1992–1999), and the University of Pavia (~1999).

Silvio Vita specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, studying at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton University. He directed the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~2001–2023) and was a professor at the University of Naples Federico II (~2000–2023).

Simo Parpola is a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology who earned his PhD from the University of Helsinki. He was an associate professor at the University of Chicago (1977–1979) and became a professor at Helsinki in 1978.

Simon Cubelic is an Indologist. He held posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2018) and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, where his post as professor is attested in 2026.

Simon P. James works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Durham University, serving as a tutor in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and lecturer in philosophy (attested 2013–2014).
Simon Winant works in Indology and linguistics. Attested in 2026, he is a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.
Singhathon Narāsabho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Visva-Bharati University under the doctoral supervision of Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti.
Siniruddha Dash is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as director at the University of Madras (2000–2014) and later as director of the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation in 2020.

Siran Upendra Deraniyagala was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, the University of London under Frank Raymond Allchin, and Harvard University. He was Director General of Sri Lanka's Department of Archaeology (~1992–2001).

Sisir Roy works in philosophy, having studied under Debabrata Sensharma. He has served as a professor at the Indian Statistical Institute and held a post at the National Institute of Advanced Studies (attested 2009).
Sita Krishna Nambiar is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Bonn under the doctoral supervision of Paul Hacker.

Sita Ram Roy was an archaeologist and Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Anant Sadashiv Altekar and Ram Sharan Sharma. He was a research fellow at K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute and a curator at Gaya Museum (attested 1971).
Siu-tong Kwan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and was also taught by Zhihua Yao.
Sivadatta Sarma was an Indologist who taught Sanskrit at Maharaja Sanskrit College, Jaipur, where he was attested in 1892 and 1929.

Sivananda Saraswati was a figure in philosophy and religious studies who studied at Thanjavur Medical College (~1903–1905). He founded the Divine Life Society in 1936 and the Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy in 1948.
Siyong Liang was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Tsinghua University and Harvard University (~1925–1930).
